question: A man buys magazines in bulk for ₹20 each. He sells them for ₹23 each. Find the profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price (CP) to Selling Price (SP) = 20 : 23

Profit in terms of ratio parts = 23 − 20 = 3 parts

Profit % = (Profit parts ÷ CP parts) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (3 ÷ 20) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the magazine = ₹20

Selling Price (SP) of the magazine = ₹23

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ₹20
 
 
• 
 + ₹3 (Profit)
 
 
 SP = ₹23
 
 Profit % = (3 / 20) × 100 = 15%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = 23 − 20

⇒ Profit = ₹3

⇒ Profit % = (3 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 3 × 5

⇒ Profit % = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

If Cost Price > Selling Price, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both profit and loss are always calculated on the base Cost Price (CP) unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer uses false weights to cheat the customer, his true Profit % is calculated using the formula: Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
